summary.text: Thermal radiation is electromagnetic radiation given off by the random motion of particles in any matter that is warmer than absolute zero.
At room temperature most of it is infrared, but above about 525 °C enough becomes visible that the matter glows.
It is how the Sun heats the Earth, and like light it keeps travelling through a vacuum.

facts.label: Thermal cameras
facts.value: They sense infrared to show temperature differences

facts.label: Perfect emitter
facts.value: A black body has an emissivity of one

facts.label: Sun's surface
facts.value: About 6000 K, radiating mostly visible light

items.prompt: A thermal camera picks out a person standing in a pitch-black room. Why can it see them?

options.label: Their skin reflects stray visible light
Their body gives off infrared because of its temperature
The camera sends out heat beams that bounce back
Warmth from them conducts through the air to the lens

items.explain: Thermographic cameras sense infrared radiation, and a body emits it at its own temperature, so people show up against cooler surroundings.

items.prompt: A blacksmith heats a bar of iron until it glows orange. What changed?

options.label: It began giving off radiation for the first time
It stopped giving off infrared altogether
Enough of its emission moved into visible light
Its atoms stopped moving randomly

items.explain: All matter radiates, mostly as infrared when cool, but above about 525 °C enough of it is visible for the matter to glow.

items.prompt: A friend says a block of ice gives off no thermal radiation because it is not hot. Is that right?

options.label: Yes, since only hot objects radiate
Yes, since ice just reflects radiation instead
No, but it radiates only visible light
No, since everything warmer than absolute zero radiates

items.explain: Every bit of matter with a temperature above absolute zero emits thermal radiation, however cold it feels.

items.prompt: Physicists imagine a surface that soaks up all radiation hitting it at every wavelength. What else is true of it?

options.label: It is a perfect emitter too
It gives off no radiation at all
It only emits visible light
It stays at absolute zero

items.explain: A body that absorbs perfectly at all wavelengths, in equilibrium, is a black body, and a black body is also a perfect emitter.

items.prompt: The Sun's surface radiates mostly visible light, while Earth's surface radiates at lower frequencies. What explains the difference?

options.label: The Sun is made of different atoms than Earth
Space filters out the Earth's higher frequencies
Earth only reflects light and never emits any
The Sun is far hotter, and temperature sets the spectrum

items.explain: Temperature determines the wavelength distribution, with the peak frequency proportional to absolute temperature: about 6000 K for the Sun against roughly 300 K for Earth's surface.

items.prompt: Space between the Sun and Earth is nearly empty. How does the Sun's warmth still reach us?

options.label: Through hot air rising from the Sun's surface
Through the thin gas that fills all of space
Through electromagnetic radiation crossing the vacuum
Through direct contact between the two bodies

items.explain: Thermal radiation is the main way the Sun transfers heat to Earth, and electromagnetic radiation propagates indefinitely in a vacuum.
